message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights (Texas) | Notes | |----------|------------------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent as a security deposit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize any deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition; repair structural defects, plumbing, heating, etc.
• Must keep common areas clean and free of hazards. | If landlord fails to fix major issues, tenants may withhold rent or pursue repairs themselves (with proper notice). | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb your peaceful use of the property without reasonable cause. | Includes unlawful entry, excessive noise, or harassment. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑renewal or termination of month‑to‑month tenancy: 30 days’ written notice.
• For eviction due to nonpayment or lease violation: 3 days’ written notice (for nonpayment) or 10 days’ written notice (for other violations).
• For lease termination by landlord: 60 days’ notice for most residential leases. | Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Rent Control / Increase Limits** | • No statewide rent control; landlords can raise rent at lease renewal or with proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | Some cities may have local ordinances, but none exist in Texas. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If landlord fails to make necessary repairs after notice, tenant may pay for repairs and deduct cost from rent (up to $500 per year). | Must give landlord written notice and keep receipts. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for leases longer than one year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “no smoking”) are enforceable only if they comply with local ordinances and are not discriminatory. | Discrimination against protected classes (race, religion, disability, etc.) is illegal. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination in housing based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability, source of income, etc. | Applies to all aspects of renting, including advertising, leasing, and terms. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a complaint in court and follow proper legal procedure.
• Tenants have the right to contest eviction in court. | Evictions for nonpayment or lease violations require a formal lawsuit. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must provide reasonable notice before entering the unit (typically 24 hours).
• Exceptions include emergencies or urgent repairs. | Entry without notice can be considered trespassing. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must ensure essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) are available unless otherwise specified in lease. | Tenants may be responsible for certain utilities if stated in lease. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Tenants may sublet or assign lease with landlord’s consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld. | Consent must be in writing. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord responsible for maintaining common areas (hallways, stairwells, parking lots). | Tenants should report maintenance issues promptly. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Ensure it complies with Texas law and does not contain prohibited clauses. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of notices, emails, text messages, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 3. **Give Written Notice** – When giving notice to terminate or when requesting repairs, always do so in writing and keep proof of delivery. 4. **Know Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) may have additional tenant protection ordinances. 5. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you face eviction or disputes, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or attorney. --- #### Quick Reference: Notice Periods | Situation | Required Notice | Who Provides Notice | |-----------|-----------------|---------------------| | Landlord terminates month‑to‑month lease | 30 days | Landlord | | Landlord evicts for nonpayment | 3 days | Landlord | | Landlord evicts for other lease violations | 10 days | Landlord | | Landlord wants to increase rent (month‑to‑month) | 30 days | Landlord | | Landlord wants to increase rent (fixed-term lease) | 30 days | Landlord (must be in writing) | If you’re unsure whether a clause or action is lawful, consult the Texas Property Code or a qualified attorney.
